clue.text: Sailing-ship, highly ornate though not old

indicators.note: the ornate word is wanted without the letter for old, so one piece is dropped

parts.note: baroque describes elaborately decorated art or architecture

explanation.surface: A description of a richly decorated sailing vessel that happens to be new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not' removes the O (old) from BAROQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a three-masted vessel, a type of sailing craft.

clue.text: Bank is supported by head's plain speaking

indicators.note: in a down entry the bank sits on top of the head, held up by it

parts.note: a bluff is a steep bank or cliff
a ness is a headland, so a head

explanation.surface: A bank's frankness backed by the head office.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness means headland in British place names such as Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluffness is blunt frankness, a hearty directness of manner.

clue.text: Contribute to notes included in circular

indicators.note: two musical notes are put inside the word for circular

parts.note: round means circular
E and D are both notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Notes added to a circular letter make a contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts E and D inside ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To redound to someone's credit is to contribute to it.

clue.text: Lacking force in the campus — mostly in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray signals the letters are jumbled out of order
mostly means the last letter of campus is lost

explanation.surface: Feeble student life on a university site, largely a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'times' is an OCR slip; the scan has a dash. 'mostly' cuts CAMPUS to CAMPU, and 'in disarray' rearranges INTHECAMPU.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemphatic speech is mild and without stress, so it has no forcefulness.

clue.text: Main ploy, perhaps, of the lofty

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of main ploy could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A remark about the chief stratagem of haughty, high-minded people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange MAINPLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympian means godlike, belonging to the lofty gods on Mount Olympus or lofty in manner.

clue.text: Garland put on horse leaving one city for another

indicators.note: in a down entry the garland sits on top of what follows

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

indicators.note: the letter for horse departs from the city name

parts.note: Chester is a city in Cheshire, England
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: Garlanding a horse as it travels from one city to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H; 'leaving' removes that letter. 'another' is the definition: a second English city, distinct from the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is an English city, a different one from Chester.

clue.text: Grape-juice is an essential requirement

explanation.surface: A claim that fresh grape juice is indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: Must is unfermented grape juice for wine making; a must is also something indispensable.

clue.text: Persian queen captured by a Scotsman

indicators.note: the queen is held inside the man's name

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name
a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A queen of Persia taken prisoner by a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' looks like a cat breed in the surface but is the definition; the queen is an Indian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the old name of Iran, so a Persian is a native of that country.

clue.text: Famous college set up on the top of Dartmoor

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed college sits on the following letter
in a down entry set up means the college name is read upwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

indicators.note: the top of means the first letter of Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A renowned college built on the highest part of Dartmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ETON into NOTE; 'the top of' gives D. Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: Goddess lives with prophet

parts.note: is means exists, i.e. lives
Is. is the abbreviation for Isaiah, a prophet

explanation.surface: A goddess sharing a home with a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a principal Egyptian deity, sister and wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Strip where peacekeepers line up

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces come from the United Nations
to dress ranks is the military term for lining up soldiers

explanation.surface: Asking where the peacekeeping troops form ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: In drill, troops 'dress' when they straighten their line.
explanation.definitionFit: To undress is to take one's clothes off, a verb meaning strip.

clue.text: The second of this month?

explanation.surface: A question about the date: is it the second of the current month?
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a brief moment, like a second; in old business letters 'instant' (inst.) means of the present month.

clue.text: In favour of advertisement about posh bed

indicators.note: the charade of the two pieces goes around the letter for posh

parts.note: being for something means being in favour of it
U is the old British label for upper-class usage, so posh
a poster is a printed advert put up on a wall

explanation.surface: Supporting an advertisement for a fancy bed.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' labels for upper-class and other British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-poster is a large bed with a pillar at each corner.

clue.text: Friendly youngster in Monchen Gladbach

explanation.surface: A remark about an amiable young person in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: Mönchengladbach is a city in Germany, so the youngster there is called by the German word for child.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means friendly and benevolent; in German, Kind is the word for a child.

clue.text: Fellow redcap attending disturbance is from the same country

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker
redcap is British slang for a military policeman, an MP
at means present at, attending
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A military policeman at a riot turns out to be a fellow countryman.
explanation.walkthrough: British military police wear red caps, hence 'redcap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Compatriot as an adjective means sharing a native land.

clue.text: Standing up to give tips about fashion

indicators.note: the word for tips goes around the word for fashion

parts.note: the ends of something are its tips
a way of doing something is its fashion or manner

explanation.surface: Fashion advice delivered while on one's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing up' is an adverb phrase here, meaning upright, not a verb of rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Endways means with the end upwards, i.e. upright, standing on end.

clue.text: Match this undeveloped setting for a poem!

indicators.note: the word for undeveloped forms a setting into which the poem is placed

parts.note: seminal means at a rudimentary stage, undeveloped
If is the poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: Matching an unfinished musical setting to a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting for' puts IF (Kipling's poem) into SEMINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is a match whose winner goes through to the final.

clue.text: Defeat heavily, no truce having been arranged

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of no truce are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A crushing defeat because no ceasefire was agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been arranged' rearranges NOTRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat an opponent soundly.

clue.text: Major crisis involves senior officer in East? Good grief

indicators.note: the officer goes inside the combined letters for East and good grief

parts.note: Mercy! is an exclamation like Good grief!
Gen. is the abbreviation for General

explanation.surface: A dire situation involving a senior officer in the East, with an exclamation of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Good grief' read as the speaker's exclamation, but the exclamation is a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden serious crisis needing immediate action.

clue.text: A girl must change outside this sports ground

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside the girl's name
change tells us to alter the order of the letters of a and must

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, as for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl having to change her clothes outside the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges A plus MUST to give STAUM, which 'outside' wraps around the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is a large arena for athletics and sport.

clue.text: Clothing laid out by soldiers in dismay

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to appal is to dismay
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers

explanation.surface: Uniforms set out by troops who are in a state of alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps, a common crossword source of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments.

clue.text: Put back two sorts of material

parts.note: rep is a ribbed woven fabric
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Returning a couple of kinds of fabric to where they came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to restore it to its place.

clue.text: Alcock, for one, found a way over the peak

indicators.note: in a down entry the a and the way sit over the peak

parts.note: via is Latin for way, a road
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: The pioneer airman Alcock finding a route over a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: John Alcock flew the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919, with Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot of aircraft, of which Alcock is an example.

clue.text: Manage to take front off range

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for range is removed, since its front goes

parts.note: scope is extent or range

explanation.surface: Coping with removing the front panel from a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take front off' drops the S from SCOPE. A range is also a cooking stove, which is the picture the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to get by, a synonym of manage.

clue.text: Heavenly body — one of the Sun's attractions!

definitions.text: Heavenly body — one of the Sun's attractions!

parts.words: Heavenly body — one of the Sun's attractions!
parts.note: a celestial object drawn in by solar gravity, with a hint of a tabloid paper's pin-up as its attraction

explanation.surface: A gorgeous figure as one of a tabloid newspaper's draws.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid famous for pin-ups; here it is the star whose gravity pulls in icy bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy celestial body on an orbit pulled around by the sun's gravity.

clue.text: Throwing by cricket side is intimidating

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
putting is throwing, as in putting the shot

explanation.surface: A cricket team's bowling is so menacing it frightens the batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side; putting the shot is an athletics throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-putting means disconcerting or discouraging, close to intimidating.

clue.text: Paid employment for a courier once

explanation.surface: A job delivering messages in olden times.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job or position; in older usage a post was a messenger carrying mail.

clue.text: Examine evidence of this if the case demands it

indicators.note: evidence of shows the letters are present within the words this if the

explanation.surface: Advice to scrutinise the evidence whenever the legal case needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across thiS IF The.
explanation.definitionFit: To sift is to examine closely, separating useful facts from the rest.

clue.text: Flighty type embracing a little green man?

indicators.note: the bird's name holds the letter a within it

parts.note: a martin is a bird, so a type that flies

explanation.surface: A fickle person hugging a small green-skinned alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' looks like fickle, but it means able to fly: a bird. 'embracing' puts A in MARTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Little green men are the stock comic picture of aliens, such as visitors from Mars.

clue.text: Struck son with glove

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogy
a mitten is a glove without separate fingers

explanation.surface: A boy hit by a glove.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the old past participle of smite, so hit.

clue.text: Tattler re-created by Rossini

explanation.surface: A gossip whose story was set to music by an Italian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini's opera William Tell re-created the story of Tell, so a 'Tell tale'.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale reveals secrets, just as a tattler gossips; Rossini's William Tell retells the legend of Tell.

clue.text: Tempestuous legend about opening of mine

indicators.note: the word for legend wraps around the start of mine

parts.note: a legend is a traditional story

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word mine is taken

explanation.surface: A dramatic tale about the opening of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside STORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather or temper is violent and turbulent.
